summary: This code creates a list of blog series by grouping posts that share a series name, then sorts each series chronologically and generates metadata for display. It handles both published and draft articles, translates series names and descriptions into the current language, and returns an array of series objects with permalinks, images, titles, and post counts.

explanations.46: A Map is a data structure that stores key-value pairs; here we'll use series names as keys and arrays of posts as values to group posts by their series.
explanations.49: This fetches all blog posts from metadata, including draft posts, so we can later count how many drafts are in each series.
explanations.56: We check if this series name already exists in our map; if not, we create a new empty array for it before adding the first post.
explanations.59: The exclamation mark tells TypeScript we're sure the series key exists in the map (we just checked it), so it won't complain about a possible undefined value.
explanations.65: We convert the map keys to an array, sort them alphabetically, then transform each series name into a full series object with all its metadata.
explanations.68: We're converting date strings to actual Date objects and comparing their numeric timestamps to sort posts from oldest to newest.
explanations.74: We're building a human-readable string that combines the published article count with a draft count suffix, both using the translate function to support multiple languages.
explanations.79: If there are no draft posts, we skip adding the 'in progress' section entirely; otherwise we append it with a bullet separator.
explanations.93: We use the first post's image if available, otherwise fall back to the default image provided when calling this function.
